Published online:
    September 10, 2026

Geographic focus:
    Europe (primary), United States (secondary)

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [NO]
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES]
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES]

Synopsis:
    The ECB raised rates 25bps to 2.5%, citing war-driven energy inflation (Brent at $105/bbl) from a U.S.-Israeli conflict with Iran. Lagarde flagged upside inflation risks. European equities fell ~0.5%, German 10Y yields hit 2011 highs at 3.482%, and markets priced 60bps more ECB hikes by April 2027. On the US side, hotter-than-expected PPI (+5.4% annualized) rattled Wall Street, pushing Fed hike odds to 74% for the Sept 15-16 meeting. US CPI on Friday seen as the next key catalyst.

Q01. Is the content's main message on the US economy, US yields, US interest rates?
Relevance: NO — primary focus is European markets and ECB policy; US rates are a significant secondary thread

Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 65 (moderately relevant — hotter PPI and 74% priced hike probability make this a clear secondary narrative)
Probability of increase: 74%

Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?
Relevance: 15 (minor — no meaningful argument for a hold is presented)
Probability of holding: 26%

Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 0 (NO — no dovish Fed signal anywhere in the article)
Probability of decrease: 0%

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?
Sentiment: 70 (More hawkish than before — PPI beat expectations, 74% market-implied hike probability is up from prior, and Friday CPI is expected to reinforce the hawkish trajectory; no offsetting dovish signals present)
